messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — elevated 502/504 rate for CatalystCorp private deployment (dedicated pool). Observed failures originate from private gateway egress to upstream partner (vendor-psi). Failure rate ~35% over last 5m, spike starting 00:12 UTC. Root path: /v1/generate. Affected capacity: dedicated-pool-7. Pager: oncall.

alice_ops: acked. I’m on it. Can someone confirm customer-visible impact?

bob_net: looking at NLB target health — target group tg-prod-psi shows 3/8 unhealthy. Healthcheck failing with TCP reset. Also seeing SYN retransmits from gateways in subnet 10.2.3.0/24.

carol_se: customer reported increased latency then 502s — they saw roughly ~20% user requests failing in their EU region. They’re on a strict SLO, asking for ETA. PSM looped in.

dave_sre: quick triage notes: Recent security group rollout (sg-ephemeral-2026) deployed to dedicated-pool-7 at 23:58 UTC. I’m seeing logs that connections to vendor-psi's frontends are RST. Could be overly restrictive egress rule.

alice_ops: can you validate SG rules and show the diff? if it's that, we can revert or open a temporary allow rule.

dave_sre: pulling diffs now. Patch included a deny-all-everything-then-allow pattern; a missing allow for vendor CIDR 34.198.12.0/24 on 443 looks likely.

bob_net: confirmed: current ruleset for sg-ephemeral-2026: allow 10.2.0.0/16, deny all other egress. No vendor ranges. We should add a specific egress allow to the vendor CIDR on 443 and 80 as immediate mitigation.

alice_ops: agreed. Plan: 1) add temp egress rule to sg-ephemeral-2026 -> allow 34.198.12.0/24:443, 2) monitor target health + error rate for 10m, 3) if stable, start DNS weight shift to secondary region (eu-west-2 fallback), 4) schedule full rollback/perm fix after postmortem. Any objections?

carol_se: customer wants rollback of the SG change instead of add rules. Do we have safe rollback candidate and a quick test path? They prefer minimal config churn.

dave_sre: rollback is possible but one deploy step will touch many hosts; risk of knocking other fixes. Safer to add the allow now and then roll a constrained rollback if needed.

bob_net: executing temp egress update (will be very targeted). Command I’ll run:```bash
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 34.198.12.0/24 --region eu-west-1
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f --protocol tcp --port 80 --cidr 34.198.12.0/24 --region eu-west-1
```

bob_net: update — rule applied to sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f (sg-ephemeral-2026). Propagation to instances should be near-instant.

dave_sre: I’m seeing target health recover to 6/8 in the last 30s. Error rate dropped from 35% -> ~8% in logs. Great sign.

alice_ops: can we get a quick synthetic check? curl from a gateway node to vendor endpoint 

carol_se: test from gateway: ```bash
curl -I https://api.vendor-psi.example/healthz -m 5
HTTP/2 200\nserver: nginx\ndate: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 00:19:10 GMT\n
``` So vendor is reachable from gateway.

frank_support: Customer update prepared: telling them we applied a targeted egress allow and are monitoring; we propose DNS traffic shift only if instability continues. Want me to send now?

alice_ops: yes please — be explicit: mitigation applied, short-term fix, rolling monitoring window 15m, no app-level code change. Ask them to hold on any internal rollbacks until we confirm.

carol_se: noted. Sent message to customer: "We've applied a targeted networking mitigation to restore connectivity to vendor endpoints. We're seeing error rates fall; we'll continue monitoring and will coordinate any further changes with you."

dave_sre: next steps: 1) keep temp egress rule for 24h, 2) revert the deny-if-no-longer-needed pattern in next config patch and add explicit allow baseline for known vendor CIDRs, 3) create a canary for SG rollouts to avoid blast radius.

bob_net: I’ll also add an automated healthcheck in Route53 to weight-shift if target health < 60% for >5m, but only after ops signoff. Pseudocode:```json
{
  "HealthCheck": {
    "Type": "HTTPS",
    "ResourcePath": "/healthz",
    "FailureThreshold": 3
  },
  "RoutingPolicy": "weighted"
}
```

alice_ops: cool. For now we hold off on DNS changes. Let’s keep monitoring. Anyone on nightshift after 00:30 UTC? I need a handoff after 00:40.

frank_support: I’ll take handoff at 00:40 UTC. I’ll watch dashboards and alerts, and coordinate with customer if anything regresses. Please add a short summary before you leave.

dave_sre: summary for handoff -> 'Applied targeted egress allow for vendor CIDR 34.198.12.0/24 on sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f for dedicated-pool-7 at 00:18 UTC. Target health rising, error rate dropped from ~35% to ~8%. No service restarts. Monitoring window set to 15m for immediate SLO recovery.'

alice_ops: thanks. I'm stepping off in 20. leaving monitoring hooks and the runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sg-rollout-mitigation. :thumbsup:

frank_support: ack. I’ll keep the thread open and escalate to oncall-sre if anything crosses P0 thresholds. Good work team.

incident-bot: incident updated — status: mitigated (partial) — customer-facing noise reduced. Continue monitoring.
